summary: Remote WebSocket peer drives an interactive PTY, filesystem, git, and self-upgrade on the installer's host
details: The package runs a long-lived agent that connects to a configurable WebSocket server (defaulting to ws://localhost:3456 but overridable via SERVER_URL/agent-config) and routes messages from that server into privileged handlers on the installer's machine. `terminal_input` frames are written directly into a spawned PTY (bash on POSIX, PowerShell/cmd on Windows) via pty.spawn + term.pty.write, giving the remote party an interactive shell as the running user. Additional handlers (`write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `transfer_files`, `git_add`/`reset`/`restore`/`commit`/`push`, `upgrade_agent`) let the same peer rewrite arbitrary files, push git changes under the installer's identity, and trigger `npm install <pkg>@latest` followed by a systemd/launchd/PM2 service restart, providing a persistent self-upgrade channel. service/linux.js writes shell PATH modifications (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin) to persist the agent's environment. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket endpoint — or anyone reaching an unauthenticated or weakly-authenticated deployment — obtains full-host code execution, file/git mutation, and update-channel control on the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
